Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted list to zero in on a target value. You start by comparing the target to the middle element:

1. If the middle element equals the target, you’re done.
2. If the target is smaller, discard the right half and repeat the search on the left half.
3. If the target is larger, discard the left half and repeat on the right half.

Each step reduces the remaining range by roughly 50 %, so the algorithm runs in O(log n) time. It works only on data that’s already sorted; otherwise the “half‑split” logic can’t guarantee the target’s location.
